title: Exterior free etale sheaf represents alternating configuration sections
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale morphism from a scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume that $f$ is separated, meaning its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E$ be the free abelian sheaf on $U/X$: the sheafification of the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{a\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)}\mathbf Z e_a$ on etale scheme objects $V\to X$, with restriction $e_a\mapsto e_{a|_{V\prime}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $\epsilon:E\to\underline{\mathbf Z}$ send each $e_a$ to $1$. Write $\bigwedge^nE$ for the sheafification of sectionwise exterior powers over $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, with exterior powers as in [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and tensor as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $p\geq0$ put $W_p=U^{\times_X(p+1)}\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}\{u_i=u_j\}$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; each equality locus is the pullback of the diagonal. Then $W_p$ is an open and closed subscheme, etale over $X$, and coordinate permutation gives a free action of $\mathfrak S_{p+1}$ on it. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ there is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{et}})}(\bigwedge^{p+1}E,F)\cong\{s\in\Gamma(W_p,F|_{W_p}):\sigma^*s=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)s\text{ for all }\sigma\in\mathfrak S_{p+1}\}.$$ Here restriction and sections on etale algebraic spaces have their small-site meaning [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The isomorphism sends $h$ to evaluation on the wedge of the $p+1$ tautological lifts of $U$ over $W_p$. It commutes with every morphism $F\to F\prime$; in particular it identifies the cochain maps obtained by applying either side to a complex of abelian sheaves. No division by $(p+1)!$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0726, lemma-compute, including its open-and-closed distinct-locus assertion and its functorial Hom identification.

proof.text: Put $n=p+1$ and $T=U^{\times_X n}$. Repeatedly use [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to represent $T$ by a scheme (each new factor is the base change of the representable etale $U\to X$ to a scheme). Its map to $X$ is etale by base change and composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The diagonal of $U\to X$ is open and closed by [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement]. For each pair $i<j$, pull it back along $T\to U\times_X U$. The scheme base-change statements [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] make the equality locus $D_{ij}$ open and closed in $T$. Thus $W_p=T\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}D_{ij}$ is an open and closed subscheme. On every scheme test over $X$, its map is an open restriction of an etale scheme map and hence etale by [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction]. Permutations preserve the excluded union. If a nonidentity permutation fixes a tuple, choose a moved index: equality of that coordinate and the moved coordinate forces the tuple into some $D_{ij}$. Its fixed subspace in $W_p$ is therefore empty. This proves freeness, including $n=1$.

source.place: Tag 0726 (lemma-compute), proof: clopen diagonal, distinct-tuple quotient and its universal sign relations; expanded here by sectionwise evaluation and gluing.

proof.text: Let $P(V)=\mathbf Z^{(\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U))}$, so $E=P^\#$. Apply [lem-sfb-alternating-sheafification-universal-property] to the constant presheaf of rings $\mathbf Z$, its sheafification $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, $P$ and the integer $n$. Abelian sheaves are modules over $\underline{\mathbf Z}$: on locally constant integer sections the action is integer multiplication locally, glued uniquely by the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; every additive morphism preserves this action. Thus a morphism $h:\bigwedge^n E\to F$ is equivalent to a restriction-compatible family of alternating $\mathbf Z$-multilinear maps $P(V)^n\to F(V)$, with precisely the wedge evaluation formula in that node. No local freeness or finite fibre hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0726 (lemma-compute), proof: clopen diagonal, distinct-tuple quotient and its universal sign relations; expanded here by sectionwise evaluation and gluing.

proof.text: Given $h$, evaluate its corresponding alternating family on the $n$ tautological generators over $W_p$ to obtain $t_h\in F(W_p)$. Pullback along a coordinate permutation permutes these generators. The exterior relations in [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] give multiplication by $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ (write a permutation as transpositions), so $t_h$ is anti-invariant. Conversely let $t\in F(W_p)$ be anti-invariant. For a tuple $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of maps $V\to U$ over $X$, let $V_a=V\times_T W_p$, an open and closed subscheme by step 1 and the immersion base-change statements [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Define $c_V(a)\in F(V)$ by pulling back $t$ on $V_a$ and taking zero on its open complement. The two sections glue uniquely by the sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], since their intersection is empty and $F(\varnothing)=0$. Base change of this decomposition proves compatibility with restriction. Permuting $a$ leaves $V_a$ unchanged and changes the map to $W_p$ by that permutation, so $c_V(a\circ\sigma)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)c_V(a)$. If $a_i=a_j$ as maps, $V_a$ is empty and $c_V(a)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0726 (lemma-compute), proof: clopen diagonal, distinct-tuple quotient and its universal sign relations; expanded here by sectionwise evaluation and gluing.

proof.text:
For $x_i=\sum_a m_{i,a}e_a\in P(V)$ define
$$b_V(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^n m_{i,a_i}\right)c_V(a_1,\ldots,a_n).$$
All sums are finite and the coefficients of a free abelian group element are unique. This is multilinear by distributivity. If $x_i=x_j$, partition the summands by exchanging $a_i,a_j$. A summand fixed by this exchange has $a_i=a_j$ and is zero. The remaining summands pair with equal integer coefficients and opposite values of $c_V$, hence cancel. Thus $b_V$ is alternating, even when $F(V)$ has 2-torsion. Under restriction, distinct basis labels may coalesce, but expansion and distributivity collect their coefficients to give exactly the restriction of this same finite sum. Thus $(b_V)_V$ is restriction-compatible. The bijection of [lem-sfb-alternating-sheafification-universal-property] now gives a unique $h_t:\bigwedge^nE\to F$ with $h_t(e_{a_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{a_n})=c_V(a)$.

source.place: Tag 0726 (lemma-compute), proof: clopen diagonal, distinct-tuple quotient and its universal sign relations; expanded here by sectionwise evaluation and gluing.

proof.text: The map $W_p\to T$ defined by its tautological tuple factors through $W_p$ itself, so its distinct part is all of $W_p$. The construction therefore gives $t_{h_t}=t$. For the other composite start with $h$ and a tuple $a$ over $V$. On $V_a$, restriction of $h$ evaluated on the basis wedge is the pullback of $t_h$. On the complement of $V_a$, the open equality loci $a_i=a_j$ form a finite cover; on each one the wedge is zero by [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] therefore makes the evaluation zero throughout this complement. Thus it is exactly $c_V(a)$. Multilinearity gives equality on every tuple in $P(V)^n$, and the uniqueness assertion of [lem-sfb-alternating-sheafification-universal-property] gives $h_{t_h}=h$. Both constructions preserve addition, so the inverse bijections are isomorphisms of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 0726 (lemma-compute), proof: clopen diagonal, distinct-tuple quotient and its universal sign relations; expanded here by sectionwise evaluation and gluing.

proof.text: For a morphism $\phi:F\to F'$ the evaluation formula gives $t_{\phi\circ h}=\phi_{W_p}(t_h)$ directly. In the inverse construction $\phi$ commutes with restriction, sends zero to zero, and preserves each finite integer linear combination, so the same identity also respects the constructed inverse. Hence the isomorphism is natural in every abelian sheaf. Applying it to each differential $F^q\to F^{q+1}$ gives the claimed equality of cochain maps. Every formula used only integer multiplication, finite addition, restriction and gluing; no factorial was inverted.

lean.statement: theorem etale_configuration_exterior_hom {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : X.EtaleSite) (hsurj : IsSurjective U.obj.hom) (hsep : IsSeparatedPresheafMap U.obj.hom) (p : ℕ) : ∃ (T : X.EtaleSite) (pr : Fin (p + 1) → (T ⟶ U)), Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk T pr)) ∧ ∃ (W : X.EtaleSite) (j : W ⟶ T) (ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) →* Aut W), IsOpenImmersion ((X.etaleForget).map j) ∧ IsClosedImmersion ((X.etaleForget).map j) ∧ Set.range ((X.etaleForget).map j).base = configurationDistinctSet X U T (p + 1) pr ∧ (∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1))) (i : Fin (p + 1)), (ρ σ).hom ≫ j ≫ pr i = j ≫ pr (σ.symm i)) ∧ (∀ (V : Scheme.{u}) (a : V ⟶ (X.etaleForget).obj W) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1))), Nonempty V → a ≫ (X.etaleForget).map (ρ σ).hom = a → σ = 1) ∧ ∃ e : ∀ F : Sheaf X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}, (configurationExteriorSheaf X U (p + 1) ⟶ F) ≃+ configurationAntiInvariant X W (p + 1) ρ F, (∀ (F : Sheaf X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (h : configurationExteriorSheaf X U (p + 1) ⟶ F), (e F h).val = h.hom.app (op W) (configurationWedge X U W (p + 1) (fun i ↦ j ≫ pr i))) ∧ (∀ (F G : Sheaf X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (φ : F ⟶ G) (h : configurationExteriorSheaf X U (p + 1) ⟶ F), (e G (h ≫ φ)).val = φ.hom.app (op W) (e F h).val)
lean.note: The theorem jointly specifies the scheme fibre product by its product cone in the small etale site, its clopen distinct locus, the free coordinate action, and the additive Hom equivalences with tautological-wedge evaluation and naturality. The helper definitions construct the free sheaf, augmentation, integral exterior sheaf, generators, wedge, equality-locus complement and sign subgroup from Mathlib functors; no data are postponed.
